Revised assessment incorporating SLOOS: The FOMC’s December 2017 statement remains consistent with a gradualist, forward‑looking framework: solid growth and strong labor markets alongside sub‑2% inflation, symmetric 2% objective, and an implementation mix of IOER/ON RRP corridor plus balance sheet runoff. However, the October 2017 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey points to a more mixed credit backdrop than the statement alone implies. Banks eased standards for C&I lending, but tightened terms for consumer credit—especially credit card and auto loans—citing economic outlook, loan portfolio quality, and risk tolerance. SLOOS also reports weakened loan demand across several categories (credit card, auto, inventory and accounts receivable financing, investment in plant/equipment, and M&A), with competition driving some easing and banks noting willingness to make consumer installment loans. Netting this, the growth/labor tone is still moderately positive, but SLOOS‑indicated softness in consumer credit and tepid loan demand tempers optimism. Overall sentiment: slightly positive, but a notch less than before.
